note: Rodent NMDA-hypofunction models and rat CSF-glycine PD predicted that GlyT1 (SLC6A9) inhibition would treat negative and cognitive symptoms; the PD translated and both phase 2s were positive, but every phase 3 (bitopertin 2016, iclepertin 2025) failed and no member was filed.
label: Schizophrenia (GlyT1)

engagement.note: RG1678 (bitopertin) raised CSF and striatal glycine dose-dependently in rats; no human CSF read-out yet.
engagement.quote: In vivo, RG1678 dose-dependently increased cerebrospinal fluid and striatal levels of glycine measured by microdialysis in rats.
engagement.judgement: Dated 2011 by the online date (27 Nov 2011); print is Feb 2012. Roche's earlier internal PD work is unpublished, so this is the first public use of the rat CSF-glycine biomarker for a member drug.

engagement.note: Healthy volunteers on 3-60 mg bitopertin: CSF glycine rose dose-dependently to 2.3x at 60 mg; Roche states the maximum matched the animal data.
engagement.short: Human CSF glycine rose as in rats
engagement.quote: The maximal increase observed in healthy volunteers was similar to the one observed in animals showing the good translatability of this biomarker.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the animal maximum is not numbered in the abstract, so within_2x rests on the authors' 'similar'.
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison by the sponsor, healthy volunteers not patients. The human study ran 2008-2010 but was public only in May 2016, which sets the year; a reader who dates by Umbricht 2014's occupancy-efficacy sentence would put engagement at 2014 on the occupancy track instead.
engagement.magnitude_basis: maximal CSF glycine rise (human 2.3x at 60 mg vs rat microdialysis maximum, called similar)

engagement.note: Iclepertin: rat CSF glycine +30-78% (0.2-2 mg/kg); healthy volunteers +50% at 10 mg, the dose later taken into phase 3.
engagement.short: Iclepertin CSF glycine translated rat to human
engagement.quote: Similarly, oral administration of BI 425809 in healthy volunteers resulted in a dose-dependent increase in glycine CSF levels at steady state, with a mean 50% increase at doses as low as 10 mg.
engagement.reason: CSF glycine rose in humans as in rats
engagement.judgement: Iclepertin is its own track on the rat CSF-glycine system (opener appended as engagement 8); first comparison on that track. Registry record of the human CSF study (NCT02362516) posted results only on 2026-03-30; the paper (online 23 Aug 2018) sets the year.
engagement.magnitude_basis: CSF glycine rise: rat 78% at 2 mg/kg vs human 50% at 10 mg

engagement.note: Baboon PET with the clinical tracer put 50% GlyT1 occupancy at ~150-300 ng/mL bitopertin plasma; no human occupancy yet.
engagement.quote: Plasma concentrations of approximately 150-300 ng/mL were estimated to produce 50% GlyT1 occupancy in the thalamus, the cerebellum and the pons.
engagement.judgement: Online 10 Dec 2011, print July 2013. A different system from the rat microdialysis track (primate PET, direct occupancy), so its own track.

engagement.note: Healthy-volunteer PET with the same tracer: occupancy EC50 ~130-200 ng/mL, Emax ~92%, inside the baboon-predicted 150-300 ng/mL.
engagement.quote: At steady state, the relationship between bitopertin plasma concentration and GlyT1 occupancy derived by the 2T5P model, SRTM, and PRTM exhibited an EC(50) of ∼190, ∼200, and ∼130 ng/ml, respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Paired by me: the human abstract does not quote the baboon numbers.
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison (hatched): Borroni's baboon 150-300 ng/mL for 50% occupancy against the human EC50 of ~130-200 ng/mL, within 2x. Online 7 Nov 2012 sets the year. PF-03463275 later gave linear 44-83% occupancy in patients with [18F]MK-6577 (D'Souza 2018, 10.1016/j.biopsych.2017.12.019), consistent with the class engaging its target.
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma concentration for 50% GlyT1 occupancy: baboon 150-300 ng/mL vs human EC50 ~130-200 ng/mL

engagement.quote: In contrast, all doses of PF-3463275 alleviated the deficit in spatial working memory induced by ketamine.
engagement.note: PF-3463275 (0.01-0.17 mg/kg sc) reversed the ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit in rhesus at every dose, not the hallucinatory-like behaviours.
engagement.judgement: Member drug in the model (PF-3463275 is PF-03463275). First published use of the primate ketamine working-memory assay for the class; Neuroreport 31 Mar 2010.
engagement.model: Rhesus monkey ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit

engagement.quote: However, it contrasts with non-human primate (NHP) studies in which PF-03463275 and ORG-25935 reduced ketamine effects on working memory
engagement.note: In healthy volunteers PF-03463275 at 10-40 mg bid (44-76% occupancy) did not reverse ketamine-induced working-memory deficits; the source states the contrast with monkeys.
engagement.short: Human ketamine WM readout did not move
engagement.reason: Monkey reversal absent in dosed humans
engagement.judgement: The model's readout (reversal of ketamine-induced working-memory impairment) did not move in dosed humans at occupancies up to 76%; the source names the contrast and offers task over-training, infusion timing and species as reasons. A ketamine-independent accuracy gain at 40 mg is a different readout. Healthy volunteers count for engagement.
engagement.model: Rhesus monkey ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit

engagement.note: Iclepertin (BI 425809) raised rat CSF glycine 30-78% at 0.2-2 mg/kg; the rat PD that opens the iclepertin track.
engagement.short: Rat CSF glycine up with iclepertin
engagement.quote: Oral administration of BI 425809 in rats induced a dose-dependent increase of glycine CSF levels from 30% (0.2 mg/kg, not significant) to 78% (2 mg/kg, P < 0.01), relative to vehicle.
engagement.judgement: Opener for the iclepertin track of the rat CSF-glycine system, at its first public use for that drug (Rosenbrock 2018, online 23 Aug 2018); same paper as the human comparison (engagement 3).

dose.note: Bell-shaped exposure-response in rat hippocampal LTP (active at 100 nM, not 300 nM): efficacy expected at partial, not maximal, GlyT1 occupancy.
dose.short: Rat LTP: active at 100 nM, not 300 nM
dose.quote: In hippocampal CA1 pyramidal cells, RG1678 enhanced NMDA-dependent long-term potentiation at 100 nM but not at 300 nM.
dose.judgement: The dose model is the inverted-U occupancy window, not a plain exposure target: Roche selected 10-60 mg for phase 2 to span low-to-medium occupancy. No FDA filing exists for any member, so model_filed is null everywhere.

dose.note: Phase 2: 10 and 30 mg (low-to-medium occupancy) improved negative symptoms, 60 mg did not; Roche states this matched the preclinical window.
dose.quote: Estimates of bitopertin binding to glycine transporter type 1 showed that low to medium levels of occupancy yielded optimal efficacy in patients, consistent with findings in preclinical assays.
dose.confidence_note: Efficacy significant in the per-protocol population only (trend in ITT); the preclinical assays are not named in the abstract.
dose.judgement: Scored same because the window was reached and, in this trial, enough. The JAMA Psychiatry online-first date could not be confirmed, so epub_year is null and the year is the June 2014 issue; Pinard 2010 (10.1021/jm100210p) had already disclosed a phase 2 benefit without data.
dose.magnitude_basis: occupancy band giving efficacy (low-medium in both)

dose.note: Rat CSF-glycine rise for bitopertin (RG1678); Roche set bitopertin doses from the occupancy window, so this system stated no bitopertin dose target.
dose.short: Rat CSF glycine as dose target
dose.quote: In vivo, RG1678 dose-dependently increased cerebrospinal fluid and striatal levels of glycine measured by microdialysis in rats.
dose.judgement: Separate dose track from the occupancy window: a different model (CSF glycine PD) and a different prediction (a PD-defined dose for iclepertin, 10 mg). Split by drug: this entry is the bitopertin track (its quote is RG1678); the iclepertin dose track opens at dose 7.

dose.note: Iclepertin 10 mg gave the rat-defined PD target (~50% CSF glycine rise) in healthy volunteers; phase 2 then found 10 and 25 mg active.
dose.quote: Similarly, oral administration of BI 425809 in healthy volunteers resulted in a dose-dependent increase in glycine CSF levels at steady state, with a mean 50% increase at doses as low as 10 mg.
dose.judgement: Healthy-volunteer PK/PD counts. Fleischhacker 2021 (10.1016/S2215-0366(20)30513-7) confirmed 10 and 25 mg active in patients, which would be a strengthening same and is left to the efficacy cell.
dose.magnitude_basis: CSF glycine rise: rat 78% at 2 mg/kg vs human 50% at 10 mg

dose.quote: PF-03463275 increased long-term potentiation only in SZs with peak effects at 40 mg twice a day (∼75% GlyT1 occupancy) and with a profile suggestive of an inverted U dose response.
dose.note: PF-03463275 LTP peaked at 40 mg bid (~75% occupancy) with an inverted U; 60-80% occupancy was named the optimal window and set the trial doses.
dose.short: Human LTP peaked at 40 mg bid
dose.judgement: Dose-finding ran in patients themselves, so the dose model is human. Registered under NCT01911676 (first posted 2013-07-30), the same record as the later trial; the PET/LTP data are not posted there. Online 31 Jan 2018 sets the year; print Sep 2018.
dose.model: Human visual-evoked-potential LTP (EEG neuroplasticity) in schizophrenia patients

dose.quote: PF-03463275 treatment, at doses demonstrated to engage the target, was safe and well-tolerated but did not produce a greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.
dose.note: 40 and 60 mg bid, chosen from the LTP peak and highest occupancy, dosed with adherence checks; no MCCB gain over CT alone; programme ended.
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction (rule v4): 40 and 60 mg bid, chosen from the LTP peak and occupancy, were dosed. Reached, failed, abandoned: contra derived from efficacy, counted once. The trial paper sets its dose rationale beside the result ('Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores'), so the comparison is stated. Registry results (2023-02-27) precede the epub (2 May 2023); year 2023 either way.
dose.model: Human visual-evoked-potential LTP (EEG neuroplasticity) in schizophrenia patients

dose.note: Rat CSF-glycine rise with iclepertin defined the PD target (~50% rise) later used to pick the 10 mg human dose.
dose.short: Rat CSF glycine sets iclepertin PD target
dose.quote: Oral administration of BI 425809 in rats induced a dose-dependent increase of glycine CSF levels from 30% (0.2 mg/kg, not significant) to 78% (2 mg/kg, P < 0.01), relative to vehicle.
dose.judgement: Opener for the iclepertin dose track of the rat CSF-glycine system (Rosenbrock 2018); the bitopertin track of this system is dose 3.

efficacy.note: Bitopertin blocked amphetamine- and L-687,414-induced hyperlocomotion in mice and the amphetamine hyper-response of chronic-PCP rats; no patient data.
efficacy.quote: Additionally RG1678 attenuated hyperlocomotion induced by the psychostimulant d-amphetamine or the NMDA receptor glycine site antagonist L-687,414 in mice.
efficacy.judgement: The class went into patients on NMDA-hypofunction reversal screens; this is the first published member data.

efficacy.note: Phase 2 (n=323): 10 and 30 mg cut PANSS negative factor 25% vs 19% placebo in the per-protocol population; ITT trend only.
efficacy.quote: Results reached trend-level significance in the intent-to-treat population. Estimates of bitopertin binding to glycine transporter type 1 showed that low to medium levels of occupancy yielded optimal efficacy in patients, consistent with findings in preclinical assays.
efficacy.confidence_note: Primary endpoint significant in the per-protocol population, trend in ITT: scored same with source_calls_it partial.
efficacy.judgement: CandleLyte (10.1016/j.euroneuro.2014.03.007, online Mar 2014) missed PANSS total in acute exacerbation but olanzapine missed too, so it is a failed assay, not a contra, and does not change status. Pinard 2010 disclosed the phase 2 benefit without data; year stays 2014 when the endpoint became public.

patient_trials.quote: Results reached trend-level significance in the intent-to-treat population.
In summary, this study failed due to lack of statistical separation of either bitopertin or olanzapine (active control) from placebo on the primary endpoint.

efficacy.note: Phase 3 FlashLyte/DayLyte (n=1199): no dose separated on PANSS negative factor; first public in Roche's 21 Jan 2014 release, so dated 2014 (earliest public date; the 2016 paper sets the status).
efficacy.quote: These studies provide no evidence for superior efficacy of adjunctive bitopertin in any of the doses tested over placebo in patients with persistent predominant negative symptoms of schizophrenia.
efficacy.judgement: FlashLyte/DayLyte chosen because they re-tested the exact 2014 prediction, powered, at the same doses. Year 2014 under the earliest-public-date ruling: Roche's media release of 21 Jan 2014 said FlashLyte and DayLyte 'failed to meet their primary endpoints'; Bugarski-Kirola (online 15 Dec 2016, tier 1) sets the status. Dunayevich (AMG 747, online 24 Oct 2016) and SearchLyte (2 Nov 2016) are later contras. No bitopertin registry record carries results. AMG 747's two trials were terminated early for TEN, so its primary miss is underpowered and is listed, not status-setting. PF-03463275's negative-symptom trial NCT00977522 was terminated in 2010 with no results. Which of NCT01192867/NCT01192880/NCT01192906 is SunLyte, DayLyte or FlashLyte is not stated in the abstract.

patient_trials.quote: These studies provide no evidence for superior efficacy of adjunctive bitopertin in any of the doses tested over placebo in patients with persistent predominant negative symptoms of schizophrenia.
SunLyte met the prespecified criteria for lack of efficacy and was declared futile.

At week 24, mean change from baseline showed improvement in all treatment arms but no statistically significant separation from placebo in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale negative symptom factor score and all other end points.
Only one of six active treatment arms across the three studies offered an advantage of adjunctive bitopertin over placebo for the treatment of suboptimally controlled symptoms of schizophrenia.
MoonLyte was discontinued in September, 2014, on the basis of results from futility analyses.
Only one of six active treatment arms across the three studies offered an advantage of adjunctive bitopertin over placebo for the treatment of suboptimally controlled symptoms of schizophrenia.
At week 12, change from baseline NSA-16 total score showed no differences between groups.
Studies were terminated early after a report of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (SJS/TEN) in one participant (40-mg AMG 747).

efficacy.model: Rodent MK-801 cognition and EEG (T-maze, social recognition, ASSR)
efficacy.note: Iclepertin reversed MK-801 working-memory and auditory-gating deficits in rodents; published after the positive phase 2 and framed as supporting it.
efficacy.quote: These findings support previous clinical evidence for the procognitive effects of iclepertin.
efficacy.confidence_note: Whether the rodent experiments were run before Fleischhacker 2021 is not stated; the paper cites the clinical result in its introduction, so it is scored as a retrodiction. A reader satisfied that the work predated the clinic would score same.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the hyperlocomotion screens: a different model (MK-801 cognition/EEG) and a different prediction (pro-cognitive, MCCB). Boehringer's pre-FIH rodent cognition data are unpublished, so the track opens with this 2022 paper. The phase 2 it reproduces: MCCB composite +1.98 (10 mg) and +1.73 (25 mg) vs placebo, registry results 2021-02-24.

patient_trials.quote: BI 425809 improved cognition after 12 weeks in patients with schizophrenia; doses of 10 mg and 25 mg showed the largest separation from placebo.

efficacy.model: Rodent MK-801 cognition and EEG (T-maze, social recognition, ASSR)
efficacy.note: CONNEX-1/2/3 (n=1835, 10 mg, 26 weeks): MCCB composite difference 0.13 T-score points, p=0.63; programme terminated. Topline first public in Boehringer's January 2025 release; year unchanged.
efficacy.quote: Iclepertin was not associated with significant improvements in cognition in adults with schizophrenia, but it was well tolerated by patients.
efficacy.judgement: First prospective test after the retrodiction, scored as usual: contra. Year by the CONNEX-1 registry posting (2025-11-05); the Lancet Psychiatry online-first date was not confirmed. PF-03463275 plus cognitive training (Surti 2023, NCT01911676, results 2023-02-27) also failed on MCCB, but its dose was set from human LTP (D'Souza 2018), not a rodent model, so it is noted here rather than scored on this track.

patient_trials.quote: At week 26, there was no significant difference between treatment groups in the primary endpoint.
At week 26, there was no significant difference between treatment groups in the primary endpoint.
At week 26, there was no significant difference between treatment groups in the primary endpoint.

efficacy.quote: These findings provide support for a clinical trial to test the ability of PF-03463275 to enhance cognitive remediation toward addressing cognitive impairments associated with schizophrenia.
efficacy.note: Enhanced visual LTP in patients at 40 mg bid was read as neuroplasticity that would augment cognitive training in CIAS.
efficacy.short: Human LTP gain predicted CT augmentation
efficacy.judgement: The model's prediction is explicit: LTP enhancement should let PF-03463275 augment cognitive remediation. No patient comparison until the trial read out.
efficacy.model: Human visual-evoked-potential LTP (EEG neuroplasticity) in schizophrenia patients

efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 in combination with CT was feasible, safe, and well-tolerated at the doses prescribed but did not produce greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.

patient_trials.quote: Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores in patients receiving CT.

efficacy.note: NCT01911676 (n=71 crossover, 5 weeks plus CT): neither 40 nor 60 mg bid improved the primary MCCB composite over CT alone. Design: drug vs placebo, both arms with cognitive training (not a drug partner), scored on the primary.
efficacy.reason: Human LTP positive; MCCB trial flat
efficacy.judgement: A member's own human model with a prospective dose and efficacy test: it said 40 mg bid enhances neuroplasticity and should augment CT; the primary MCCB composite did not move at 40 or 60 mg. The source leaves the LTP-to-cognition link open ('further research is necessary to directly and conclusively link GLYT1 occupancy and/or LTP with the primary outcome'), hence unresolved. The trial's own day-7 LTP replication is 'to be reported elsewhere', so no engagement entry. Separate track from the rodent systems: different model and a different prediction (neuroplasticity augmenting CT, not symptom reversal).
efficacy.model: Human visual-evoked-potential LTP (EEG neuroplasticity) in schizophrenia patients

efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 did not attenuate any ketamine-induced effects but did improve working memory accuracy in healthy control subjects.
efficacy.note: At 10-40 mg bid PF-03463275 did not attenuate ketamine-induced working-memory circuit disruption, accuracy or symptom effects in healthy volunteers; the assay predicted no NMDA-R facilitation.
efficacy.judgement: Prediction of no effect on the assay's primary endpoint (ketamine-disrupted working-memory activation). A secondary, ketamine-independent accuracy gain at 40 mg is the one positive signal. The authors questioned the assay ('the current data question the utility of the reversal of ketamine effects as an assay') and proceeded on the LTP result. Registered under NCT01911676; data not posted there.
efficacy.model: Human ketamine-challenge working-memory fMRI in healthy volunteers

efficacy.magnitude_basis: presence of a pro-cognitive effect (none in the assay, none on the MCCB primary)
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: Surti 2023 lists the ketamine fMRI among its dose-selection inputs but does not set the null result beside the trial outcome. neg rests on the assay's own positive-call bar because the class has no successful drug to define class_threshold; same + direction_only is the alternative reading.
efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 in combination with CT was feasible, safe, and well-tolerated at the doses prescribed but did not produce greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.

patient_trials.quote: Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores in patients receiving CT.

efficacy.effect_size: 0: no attenuation of any ketamine-induced effect (working-memory activation, accuracy, reaction time, PANSS) at 10-40 mg bid in healthy volunteers
efficacy.class_threshold: attenuation of ketamine-induced working-memory disruption, the assay's positive call; no member drug has met it in humans, so the bar is the assay's own criterion rather than a successful member's effect size
efficacy.note: The assay flagged PF-03463275 as inactive on NMDA-R facilitation; the drug then gave no MCCB benefit over CT alone in NCT01911676. Design: drug vs placebo, both arms with cognitive training (not a drug partner), scored on the primary.
efficacy.judgement: A model that predicted no effect for a drug that then failed: neg (matched, including a known failure), judged on what the data showed (decision 13). The ketamine-independent accuracy gain at 40 mg pointed the other way and is why the programme continued, but it is not the assay's primary readout. Org 25935's human ketamine challenge (D'Souza 2012) is the same system on a non-member and is not scored.
efficacy.model: Human ketamine-challenge working-memory fMRI in healthy volunteers

efficacy.quote: In contrast, all doses of PF-3463275 alleviated the deficit in spatial working memory induced by ketamine.
efficacy.note: Reversal of ketamine-induced working-memory deficits in rhesus was offered as translational support for GlyT1 inhibition as adjunctive treatment of cognitive dysfunction in schizophrenia.
efficacy.judgement: Prospective: eight years before the drug's human dose-finding and thirteen before its patient trial.
efficacy.model: Rhesus monkey ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit

efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: Surti 2023 does not cite the primate study; the only stated primate-versus-human comparison is D'Souza 2018 in healthy volunteers (engagement cell).
efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 in combination with CT was feasible, safe, and well-tolerated at the doses prescribed but did not produce greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.

patient_trials.quote: Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores in patients receiving CT.

efficacy.note: PF-03463275 at 40 or 60 mg bid plus cognitive training gave no MCCB benefit over CT alone (NCT01911676, n=71). Design: drug vs placebo, both arms with cognitive training (not a drug partner), scored on the primary.
efficacy.reason: Monkey WM reversal; patients no gain
efficacy.judgement: Different system from the rodent NMDA-antagonist tracks (primate, ketamine, delayed-response working memory, member drug dosed) and a prospective prediction from 2010, so its own track under this run's rule. Its human translation was already contradicted in 2018; the patient trial confirms.
efficacy.model: Rhesus monkey ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit

safety.note: PF-03463275 cut rat ERG oscillatory potentials up to ~70%, tracking vitreous level; predicts visual disturbance. No PF-03463275 patient visual data found.
safety.quote: We conclude that inhibition of the GlyT1 transporter in the retina causes ERG changes which may underlie recent reports of visual disturbance with GlyT1 inhibitors in clinical trials.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the clinical reports it refers to are not named, so subjects is null.
safety.reason: Visual harm not reported for PF-03463275
safety.judgement: Was retro. Ruling: for safety only the same drug's own earlier patient result makes a retrodiction; the source cites visual disturbance with 'GlyT1 inhibitors' in trials without naming PF-03463275, so it rests on other drugs and is undone. As a prospective harm prediction for PF-03463275 it is untested: Surti 2023 reports no AE-rate difference vs placebo (Table S3) but no visual-event count.

safety.model: Rodent haematology (haemoglobin) in pharmacology and toxicology
safety.note: Bitopertin in rats: microcytic hypochromic anaemia, haemoglobin down 20% at steady state, from glycine-limited haem synthesis.
safety.quote: GlyT1 inhibition significantly affected erythroid heme biosynthesis, manifesting as microcytic hypochromic regenerative anemia with a 20% steady-state reduction in hemoglobin.
safety.confidence_note: The abstract makes no patient comparison; the dose-dependent haemoglobin fall in bitopertin trials is in the trial papers' full texts, not quotable here.
safety.judgement: Roche's GLP toxicology, which would have shown anaemia before the 2008 phase 2, is unpublished; this 2016 Roche rat study is the first public rodent Hb datum for a member and was run after the clinical Hb signal was known, so it may itself be a retrodiction. Left untested rather than retro because the abstract states no comparison. AMG 747's SJS/TEN (trials stopped 2013) is an idiosyncratic immune harm rodents cannot show, so animal silence on it is not scored.

safety.model: Rodent haematology (haemoglobin) in pharmacology and toxicology
safety.note: Iclepertin: reversible Hb fall in rodents before the clinic; CONNEX patients (n=1835) fell 2.4 g/L by week 18 and plateaued; called a class effect.
safety.short: Rodent Hb drop appeared in patients
safety.quote: Nonclinical studies of iclepertin-treated rodents demonstrated a reversible reduction in hemoglobin versus vehicle-control animals. … In iclepertin-treated patients, hemoglobin concentration dropped within the first 18 weeks (mean change vs baseline, -2.4 g/L)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the rodent magnitude is not numbered, so direction only. Two verbatim spans joined by an ellipsis.
safety.reason: Rodent Hb drop appeared in patients
safety.judgement: Sponsor-stated nonclinical-to-clinical comparison; the iclepertin rodent work predates its 2014 first-in-human, so this is prospective, unlike the bitopertin rat study. The harm was predicted and held, so it is scored here and not as a dose toxicity block: no efficacy dose was ever limited by it. J Clin Pharmacol online date not confirmed; year by the May 2026 issue.
safety.magnitude_basis: haemoglobin fall (rodent reversible reduction, unnumbered; patients -2.4 g/L)

safety.model: Rodent haematology (haemoglobin) in pharmacology and toxicology
safety.note: Iclepertin rodent studies showed a reversible haemoglobin fall; first public in Nagy 2026, though run before the 2014 first-in-human.
safety.quote: Nonclinical studies of iclepertin-treated rodents demonstrated a reversible reduction in hemoglobin versus vehicle-control animals.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the rodent magnitude is not numbered, so direction only. Two verbatim spans joined by an ellipsis.
safety.judgement: Opener for the iclepertin track of the rodent haematology system; the rodent iclepertin data are first public in Nagy 2026 (May 2026 issue), the same source as the comparison (safety 3). The bitopertin track is safety 2.
